summary.one_liner: DeepSeek-V3 is a 671B-parameter Mixture-of-Experts language model (37B activated per token) released by DeepSeek-AI with open weights on Hugging Face, along with local inference instructions for several open-source serving frameworks.
summary.what_it_does: The README describes the DeepSeek-V3 model: a Mixture-of-Experts LLM with 671B total and 37B activated parameters per token, a 128K context length, and pre-training on 14.8T tokens followed by supervised fine-tuning and reinforcement learning. It lists two Hugging Face downloads (DeepSeek-V3-Base and DeepSeek-V3), and notes that only FP8 weights are provided, with a script (fp8_cast_bf16.py) to convert them to BF16. It includes benchmark tables comparing it against DeepSeek-V2, Qwen2.5 72B, LLaMA3.1 405B, GPT-4o and Claude-3.5-Sonnet. It also points to an official chat website and an OpenAI-compatible API platform. Local deployment options listed are the DeepSeek-Infer demo, SGLang, LMDeploy, TensorRT-LLM, vLLM, LightLLM, AMD GPUs, and Huawei Ascend NPUs, each with varying precision support.
use_cases: run a large open-weight language model locally
serve a MoE LLM with vLLM or SGLang
convert FP8 model weights to BF16
batch inference on a file of prompts
evaluate an open-source LLM against benchmarks
how_to_run: Download the model weights from Hugging Face into /path/to/DeepSeek-V3
stack: CUDA GPUs (NVIDIA H800 used for training)
notable: 671B-parameter MoE with only 37B parameters active per token
Auxiliary-loss-free load balancing strategy and Multi-Token Prediction objective, which can also be used for speculative decoding
FP8 mixed-precision training framework; only FP8 weights are released
Reasoning distilled from the DeepSeek-R1 series into DeepSeek-V3
Model weights and MIT-licensed code, with commercial use stated as supported
caveats: The DeepSeek-Infer demo is Linux with Python 3.10 only; Mac and Windows are not supported
Hugging Face Transformers is not directly supported yet, according to the README
Multi-Token Prediction support is still under development in several frameworks, and some frameworks have only partial FP8 or BF16 support

keywords: run llm on my own hardware
